name: Orbital Login
description: Restyle the wp-login.php screen with the Orbital brand — two-column layout, hero image on the left, white card with the form on the right.

sections.title: Branding
sections.description: Where the logo links and what title it carries.

sections.title: Hero image
sections.description: The big photo on the left half of the screen.

sections.title: Form copy
sections.description: Headline text above the login fields.

sections.title: Footer
sections.description: Two slots at the bottom of the form card.

settings.label: Logo link URL
settings.description: Where the login logo links to. Leave blank to keep the WordPress default (wordpress.org).

settings.label: Logo title attribute
settings.description: Title text on the login logo link. Leave blank to keep the WordPress default ("Powered by WordPress").

settings.label: Hero image
settings.description: Background image for the left half of the login screen. Leave blank to use a brand gradient.

settings.label: Photo credit text
settings.description: Shown at the bottom-left of the hero. Leave blank to hide.

settings.label: Photo credit link
settings.description: If both text and link are set, the credit becomes a link. Leave blank for plain text.

settings.label: Headline
settings.description: Greeting shown above the login form. Leave blank to hide.

settings.label: Footer left text
settings.description: Bottom-left corner of the form card. Plain text only.

settings.label: Footer right text
settings.description: Bottom-right corner of the form card. Plain text only.

settings.label: Remember the last user on this device
settings.description: After a successful login, store the username in a per-device cookie (30 days). On the next visit to wp-login.php, greet the user by name, hide the username field, and ask only for the password. Tradeoff: anyone with access to the browser learns a valid username. A 'Not you?' link clears the cookie. Password is always required — this is purely a UX shortcut.
